messages:
mike: FYI, ACME support ticket — sudden p95/p99 regression hitting their embeddings + chat endpoints around 03:00 UTC. They report p99 from ~1.8s -> ~6.2s for short requests. Attaching trace snippet in the ticket.
sara: ACK. Any deploys or config changes around that time?
raj: No infra deploys. I see a correlated spike in kv prefix miss rate and a bunch of eviction events on nodepool-3 starting 02:58 UTC. Possible hot-key churn.
raj: Quick metrics snapshot:
```
kv.prefix_miss_rate (nodepool-3): 0.12 -> 0.74
kv.evictions/sec: 4 -> 53
cache.kv_items_total: -18% (working set shrink)
request.p99.latency: 1.9s -> 6.3s
```
amelia: Customer traces show lots of distinct prefix keys that look like session IDs appended to user prefixes. Example header: `X-Prefix: acct-12345:session-6f7b9b4f` — entropy is huge, warmup can't keep up.
jen: That matches an earlier bug where SDKs started including ephemeral session ids in prefix metadata after the 2026-02 client push. We pushed a migration but some customers are on newer clients.
mike: So root cause hypothesis: prefix key cardinality explosion -> cache warmup starvation -> repeated KV misses -> extra backend work + queuing -> higher p95/p99. Also eviction thrash due to LRU aging under high cardinality.
raj: Repro steps (local):
```
# hammer with high-cardinality prefixes
for i in {1..20000}; do
  curl -sS -H "X-Prefix: acct-TEST:session-$i" https://api.redwood.internal/embeddings -d '{"input":"hi"}' &
done
```
Observed: steady rise in miss rate and p99 micro-bursts after 5k distinct prefixes.
amelia: Short-term mitigations we can try:
- normalize prefixes server-side to strip ephemeral session suffixes for known patterns
- increase `kv_cache.max_items_per_prefix` temporarily to reduce eviction churn
- enable staged warmup (drip) to avoid sudden hotset thrash
- apply request-level circuit: fallback to cpu model variant for affected route until warmup stabilizes
jen: I'll prepare a short-lived feature flag to enable prefix normalization for ACME tenant only. That should collapse cardinality immediately.
raj: I'll push a runtime config to nodepool-3 to set `kv.eviction_window_ms` -> 5000 (was 1000) and `kv.max_items_per_prefix` -> 3000 for the next 30m to dampen churn.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling config change to nodepool-3 starting 6789012420
mike: Good. Also add an alert to paging: if prefix_miss_rate > 0.4 for >5m for any tenant, route to eng-runtime oncall.
amelia: Quick note: normalization needs a safe regex whitelist to avoid collapsing real multi-tenant prefixes. Will only strip trailing `/session-<hex>` or `:session-<hex>` patterns for now.
raj: After config change at 6789012425 we saw immediate drop in eviction/sec and p99 trending down. Metrics 10m post-change:
```
kv.evictions/sec: 53 -> 9
kv.prefix_miss_rate: 0.74 -> 0.18
request.p99.latency: 6.3s -> 2.1s
```
mike: Not fully back to baseline but much better. Keep monitoring for 1h, then we can roll normalization to more tenants.
jen: Deployed tenant-scoped normalization flag at 6789012500 for ACME. Customer confirms latency improved in their staging and prod.
amelia: Follow-ups:
- SDK team to patch client so it doesn't surface ephemeral session ids in prefix by default (tracked in GH #1240)
- infra: consider adaptive eviction policy that accounts for prefix cardinality
- product: notify ACME support and document the workaround
jen: I'll handle the ACME reply and include repro notes and a temporary mitigation summary.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag toggle for ACME normalization enabled at 6789012503
mike: Closing loop: set postmortem owner? Amelia for normalization PR + Raj for eviction policy proposal. Jen to update support ticket.
amelia: I'll open a short RFC for server-side prefix canonicalization patterns and add unit tests for false-positive collapse cases.
raj: I'll run a synthetic job tomorrow that replays high-cardinality prefix traffic against our warmup heuristics to validate the new eviction-window default.
jen: Support ticket updated; customer ok with normalization and wants an ETA on SDK fix.
mike: Thanks all. Leaving thread open for monitoring notes. If p99 creeps above 3s again we escalate to oncall.
ops-bot: monitor-bot: alert suppressed for ACME for 30m (maintenance window) at 6789012600
